newsitem.title: USA: FBI breaks up New York fake marriage ring.
newsitem.headline: FBI breaks up New York fake marriage ring.

text.p: The FBI has smashed a ring that provided "brides for rent" to marry men they did not know in an attempt to circumvent new immigration laws, officials said on Friday.
Investigators arrested two women and four men in Brentwood on Long Island on Thursday and charged them with fraud for allegedly arranging fake marriages, an FBI spokesman said.

He said the matchmaking ring charged immigrants as much as $6,000 to find willing spouses. An anonymous tip led agents to the ring and they infiltrated it by working undercover with two women who were allegedly bribed to become brides.

The arrests were made just nine days after a Federal Appeals Court cleared the way for the Justice Department to enforce tough immigration guidelines that took effect on April 1. The Illegal Immigration Reform and Immigrant Responsibility Act of 1996 increases the number of border patrol agents and makes it more difficult for arrivals to seek political asylum and easier for the government to deport illegal immigrants.

The legislation has sparked panic among immigrant communities across the nation. In major U.S. cities, there have been reports of human traffic jams at marriage bureaus as non-documented residents come to tie the knot with legal residents and citizens and of long, overnight lines outside Immigration and Naturalisation Services offices.

But immigration rights advocates say marriage to a U.S. citizen was not the solution to the dilemma faced by undocumented immigrants because tying the knot does not automatically confer legal residency or citizenship.

The FBI said it also uncovered 60 suspicious marriages in Brookhaven, New York, and numerous others in Islip, New York, during the past 15 months with the same person, whom they declined to identify, officiating at all the weddings.

Arrested on Thursday and charged with running the alleged ring were Milagros Feliciano, 53, Allison Schafmayer, 21 and Edwin Torres, 31. Three others were also charged with fraud -- Marcel Vargas, 29, Mohinder Singh, 34, and Amarjit Singh, 29.
If convicted all six face up to 10 years in jail, according to the indictment filed in federal court in the Eastern District.
